thread:
li: Quick heads-up from taiko-v2 int4 shadow bring-up: yue (Cantonese) BLEU shows a 4.6 point regression on vertical subtitle set; hebrew-rtl outputs sometimes show parenthesis getting duplicated/omitted. Noting this here before we escalate. :warning:

sana: Oof. Is this on the grouping quant config (group=32) or qmap fallback? Which eval harness?

li: Run snippet:
```
python -m eval.multilang --model taiko-v2 --quant int4 --quant-group 32 --dataset subtitles_vertical --split test --tokenizer v2026-02-14 --deterministic
```
Median metrics (5 trials):
- yue-vertical BLEU: fp16 34.2 -> int4 29.6 (-4.6)
- he-il sacreBLEU: fp16 30.1 -> int4 29.4 (-0.7) but we see weird paren drops in ~12% of samples

rod: Can you paste one failing yue example & the raw token sequences? I want to check ZWSP/ZWJ handling with our packed-vocab remap.

li: Example yue source (short): "漢字\n(字幕)" (vertical layout markers present)
fp16 pred: "漢字\u200b\n（字幕）"
int4 pred: "漢字\n（字幕）"  <-- character shift: '字' moved inside parentheses and order scrambled relative to ruby tag boundary

li: Raw tokens (around span) fp16:
['U+6F22', 'U+5B57', 'U+200B', 'U+000A', 'U+FF08', 'U+5B57', 'U+5F62', 'U+FF09']
int4:
['U+6F22U+5B57U+200B', 'U+000A', 'U+FF08U+5B57', 'U+5F62', 'U+FF09']

ash: Hmm token merge at pack boundary again. We saw similar patterns but not with yue verticals. Is the tokenizer artifact identical across containers? CI uses v2026-02-14 but worker image maybe has v2026-02-20 baked in.

sana: Also note int4 runtime applies "kv-cache compacting" optimization for shortctx verticals (opt flag kv_compact=1). That path was added to save memory; might affect decode when token boundaries change. 

rod: For he-il paren duplication/omission: paste one minimal case please. Could be bidi mirror step or normalization timing.

li: Minimal he-il case: source "(שלום)"
fp16: "(שלום)"
int4: "(שלום"  <-- closing parenthesis missing in render on some outputs

ash: Missing closing paren suggests detokenize step might drop trailing punctuation if token boundaries are merged and we do an early trim. Maybe int4 detok fastpath strips what it thinks is stray whitespace codepoint.

ops-bot: shadow-run: taiko-v2:int4 created on staging-shadow-09. artifacts: https://ci.redwood/shadow/4421 :information_source:

li: I ran token-diff across 150 failing yue samples: 78% show merges at U+200B/ZWSP and 21% show extra merges at EOL markers. For he-il failures 11% show final bracket token missing pre-detok. Attached: /mnt/triage/taiko_v2_int4_yue_he_il_fails/3280007777.tar.gz

rod: Two quick repro checks: (1) force tokenizer artifact to canonical v2026-02-14 in the staging image and re-run; (2) run "weight-only" quant (weights int4, activations fp16) with kv_compact=0 to isolate kv-cache compacting effect. If (2) fixes it -> runtime bug. If (1) fixes it -> artifact drift.

li: Did (1): when forcing tokenizer v2026-02-14 BLEU improved by ~0.9 points but regression persisted. Did (2) locally: weight-only + kv_compact=0 -> BLEU recovered to within 0.4 of fp16 on a 30-sample smoke run. So kv_compact path is suspicious.

ash: Good find. That narrows it down to kv cache compacting interacting badly with packed token ids produced by int4 vocab remap. Maybe compaction uses byte offsets assuming unmerged tokens.

rod: Action items:
- ash: add small fix to kv_compact code to validate token boundaries before compaction (quick guard) and ship hotfix to staging-shadow-09.
- sana: add a tokenization-consistency check to onboarding CI: run token_diff on the smoke set against canonical tokenizer and fail builds >0.5% mismatch (this prevents silent artifact drift).
- li: upload 150-sample CSV & sample tarball to /mnt/triage and link to bug (BUG-4671).
- ops: pin tokenizer artifact in staging images to canonical release; prevent implicit latest layering.

ops-bot: BUG-4671 created: https://tracker.redwood/bugs/4671 assigned to ash.

li: One more note: he-il missing paren sometimes only on sequences where final token id was in the "packed boundary" bucket (ids %32 == 31). Could be an off-by-one during compaction buffer write.

rod: I'll review compaction buffer writes tomorrow morning. For now we should block int4 rollout for taiko-v2 and revert the integration until guard landed.

sana: Agreed. Also let's add a small RTL bracket mirror unit test that runs in the quant CI matrix. Saves support tickets.

li: Thanks all, uploading logs + deltas now. I'll post the weight-only full-run tomorrow. :thumbsup:
